Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon). The user (platform owner) has explicitly authorized fixing a live customer server's crash loop. Full context from prior diagnosis (already done, read-only):

Server "projectzomboid-kc0kcr" (VM ID 121, host 51.79.162.96, SSH port 20020) is crash-looping because its root disk (`/dev/sda1`, 77G) is 100% full. Confirmed breakdown:
- ~28 GB: Docker's json-file log for the `projectzomboid` container (id starting `3d2a7bad`) — no max-size/max-file cap was ever configured, so it grew unbounded across repeated crash-loop restarts.
- ~28.5 GB: `/var/log/syslog` + `/var/log/syslog.1` — pure spam from rsyslog logging its own "no space left on device" write failures in a feedback loop once the disk filled.
- ~11 GB: legitimate game data under `/opt/projectzomboid` (binaries, mods, the real save file) — do NOT touch this, it's fine and correctly sized for the 80GB Pro plan.

YOUR TASK — two parts:

**Part 1: Live remediation (authorized, go ahead)**
1. SSH into that VM (port 20020) and truncate the bloated Docker container log file (e.g. `truncate -s 0 /var/lib/docker/containers/3d2a7bad*/​*-json.log` — confirm the exact path first via `docker inspect --format '{{.LogPath}}' <container>`. Do NOT delete the file, truncate it in place so Docker's open file handle stays valid).
2. Clear/rotate `/var/log/syslog` and `/var/log/syslog.1` (truncate, don't delete — same reasoning, some processes may hold an open handle to syslog).
3. Confirm `df -h /` now shows real free space.
4. Restart the projectzomboid game service/container (check how this is normally done in this codebase — there should be a `gamePower`/restart action in `lib/game-control.ts` or similar; use the platform's own normal restart mechanism rather than raw docker commands if one exists, so job/state tracking stays consistent — check CLAUDE.md and existing worker code for the sanctioned way to restart a customer's game server).
5. Verify the container actually comes up healthy this time (docker ps shows it running/healthy, logs show the game server actually starting rather than immediately erroring, systemd restart counter stops climbing).
6. Confirm via the DB that the server's real status reflects reality afterward.

**Part 2: Systemic fix for future provisions (code change, normal deploy pipeline)**
The root cause that let this happen at all: whatever generates the docker run command / setupScript for game server containers (check `prisma/catalog.ts` — same file touched in a recent past session for CS2 — and/or wherever the docker run invocation is templated, e.g. worker provisioning code) does not set `--log-opt max-size=... --log-opt max-file=...` on any game container. Add a sane cap (e.g. `max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3`, ~30MB cap per container, following whatever convention/style exists elsewhere in that file) to the shared docker run template so this can't recur for ANY game family, not just Project Zomboid. If the run command differs per-family (separate setupScript entries per game like the CS2 one), find the common construction point and add it there efficiently rather than editing every single game's entry individually — but if there's truly no shared point and each game's setupScript is fully independent, then editing each one is fine, just say so.

Important: this is a change to job/container behavior for ALL customers' future server provisions — after implementing, follow this repo's established deploy discipline (git commit -> push -> deploy-staging.sh -> verify HTTP 200 -> promote-production.sh -> verify HTTP 200 AND a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID, not a stale-looking one). Do NOT re-provision or restart any OTHER existing customer's server to apply this — it only needs to affect future provisions from now on (adding a log cap to an already-running container is a nice-to-have but out of scope here; just fix it going forward).

Do NOT touch cs2-dbhy4p or any other server. Do NOT rotate any credentials. Do NOT send any customer/ticket communications.

Report back concisely: whether projectzomboid-kc0kcr is confirmed healthy now, exact commands run, and confirmation the systemic log-cap fix is deployed to production and will apply to new provisions.

**Context**: owner asked to verify every game catalog provisioning end-to-end — not just connectivity,
but actually changing configs post-provision and confirming they take effect, since that's where past
customer issues actually came from. Launched as a background agent (task id `a6a056522a5720333`,
~6h runtime, 500 tool calls, 578k tokens). It provisioned each family for real on node-2, verified
external reachability, verified a real settings-apply round-trip, then tore down before moving on.

**Result: 10 of 47 families fully swept, 9 real bugs found, 8 shipped to prod same session.**
Verified independently (not just trusted the agent's own report): all 9 commit hashes exist in
`git log` on `/opt/nxeon`, HEAD matches the working tree with no stray changes from this work, prod's
`nxeon-web` last restarted (11:02 UTC) after the last of these commits landed (10:45 UTC), and
`REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` in `worker/game-config.ts` is confirmed live as
`["palworld", "minecraft", "rust", "valheim"]`.

**The bugs, in the order they matter:**
1. **Security**: 8 game families (rust, ark, projectzomboid, etc.) auto-forwarded their RCON/admin
   port to the internet during the health-check step and never retracted it — and the underlying
   images ship default admin credentials (`docker`, `changeme12`) nothing ever overrides. Confirmed
   live off-box: a freshly provisioned Rust server's RCON answered a full `serverinfo` dump from
   outside. Fixed (`196e5c9`) by retracting the admin-port forward once the health-check that needed
   it is done — the platform's own RCON tooling tunnels over SSH and never needed the public forward
   at all. No customer was exposed (the one live Rust server predates auto-forwarding), but the next
   order of any of the 8 would have been.
2. **Same class, different angle** (`3be5383`): those same 8 families were handing customers their
   RCON port as the "join" address, not the actual game port — `GAME_PORT` was being used as both the
   health-check target and the customer-facing port, when it's only correct for the former. Same root
   cause the live customer `rust-w75hko` outage (found migrating that VM to node-2) turned out to be.
3. **Production regression from a *different*, concurrent Claude Code session** (`c59d9bc`, fixed by
   `b13b2ab`): a same-day commit sized new game VMs from the catalog's advertised numbers instead of
   `Math.max(gamePlan, basePlan)`. Correct for RAM/cores, but shrank disk on 116 of 121 plans and broke
   Project Zomboid within hours (`No space left on device` at 91.8% install, real customer impact).
   Caught because this sweep's own PZ provision hit the identical failure. This is the second time in
   one day this session's own audits caught a *different* concurrent session's regression before it
   spread further — see also [[nxeon-node1-cpu-and-devapp-relocation]] for the CPU-load side of the
   same day's concurrent-session activity.
4. Rust settings never applied (image builds its launch line from a different env-var scheme than the
   code assumed) — rewritten, verified by reading every field back off the live game via RCON
   (`66da137`). Valheim reported success while changing nothing — same shape, same fix (`206cc85`).
   Terraria could never provision at all (TShock's interactive world-selection prompt hung forever) —
   fixed with `WORLD_FILENAME` + `-autocreate` (`3c90f5d`). A 300s "big download" timeout was declaring
   healthy-but-slow installs as failed — replaced with an is-it-still-working probe (`08a16a1`+`d6fbb91`).
   vmid-skip reasons were misattributing 7 live customer VMs as orphaned backups (`7e49150`).

**RESOLVED, not an open item**: `projectzomboid-kc0kcr`'s RAM reduction (8192→6144MB) was NOT a
regression — owner confirmed (2026-09-06) it was the *correct* fix. Before `c59d9bc`, game orders
were provisioned at their linked `basePlan`'s full size instead of the advertised `gamePlan` size, so
this customer (and, per the owner, "a lot of other games") was silently *over*-delivered RAM relative
to what was actually sold — an unintended-generosity/margin bug, not a benefit owed to the customer.
`c59d9bc` correcting RAM/cores down to the advertised size was right; only its blanket application to
*disk* was wrong (games routinely need more disk than advertised, unlike RAM/cores apparently having

On 2026-09-03 at 18:44 UTC I ran `pkill -f "next start"` intending to stop only my own sandbox on
port 3010. Production (`nxeon-web`), staging (`nxeon-staging-web`) and the old sandbox all run
`npm start` → `next start`, so the pattern matched them too and all three were killed. systemd
restarted them within about one second and prod returned 200s immediately, but this was a real,
avoidable production interruption.

**Why:** every Node service on this host shares the same command line. A `-f` pattern match is not a
targeted kill here — it is a wildcard across prod, staging and sandbox alike.

**How to apply:** stop a service by its identity, never by a command-line pattern.
- Own dev server on a known port:
  `PID=$(ss -ltnpH 'sport = :3010' | grep -oP 'pid=\K[0-9]+' | head -1); [ -n "$PID" ] && kill "$PID"`
- Anything systemd-managed: `systemctl stop <unit>` — and on this box that is a prod action needing
  sign-off, so ask first.
- Never `pkill -f` / `killall` against `node`, `next`, `npm` or any shared runtime name.

Related: [[nxeon-build-isolation]] (never build in the live prod tree) and
[[nxeon-design-system-phase2]] (the work this happened during).

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.

Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.

- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.

## No game container had a log-size cap — one crash-loop filled a customer's disk to 100% (2026-09-17)

**Live incident**: `projectzomboid-kc0kcr` (VM 121) crash-looped for an extended period (systemd
`NRestarts` on its generated unit had reached 10,148) because its root disk filled completely and every
subsequent start attempt failed with `OCI runtime exec failed: ... no space left on device`. Breakdown of
the 77 GB root disk at 100%: **~28 GB** was Docker's `json-file` log for the game container — no image's
setup script has ever set `--log-opt max-size`/`max-file`, so a container restarting every few seconds
forever grows that log without bound; **~28.5 GB** was `/var/log/syslog` + `.1`, pure rsyslog spam from
logging its own "no space left on device" write failures once the disk was already full (a feedback loop,
not a separate cause); the remaining **~11 GB** was the customer's real game data (binaries/mods/save),
correctly sized and untouched.

**Live remediation** (this customer only, read-only-diagnosis-plus-truncate, no credentials touched): SSH'd
in via the platform's own `withServerSsh`/`exec` (`lib/ssh-exec.ts`, same connection path the control panel
itself uses), confirmed the exact log path with `docker inspect --format '{{.LogPath}}' <id>`, then
`truncate -s 0` (never `rm`, so Docker's and rsyslog's open file handles stayed valid) on that path and on
`/var/log/syslog`/`syslog.1`. `df -h /` went from 77G/100% used/0 avail to 22G used / 56G avail (29%).
Systemd's own `Restart=always` (see `wrapDockerGameService` below) then recovered the container on its
own once space existed — confirmed `docker ps` healthy, `NRestarts` stopped climbing, game logs showing a
real startup (workshop mod validation → world load → "Initialising Server Systems") rather than an
immediate re-crash, and the game's UDP/TCP ports actually listening. `Server.status` in the DB already
read `RUNNING` throughout and needed no correction.

**Systemic fix, for every future game provision**: `wrapDockerGameService()` in `worker/index.ts` is the
one shared point every game family's per-image `docker run -d --name X ...` setup script (defined
independently per family across `prisma/seed-wave*-games.ts`) gets rewritten through, into `docker create`
plus a generated systemd unit — see the existing 2026-08-26 entry above for why that rewrite exists at
all. It now also injects `--log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3` (a 30 MB ceiling per container,
regardless of family or how long/hard it crash-loops) into that same rewritten `docker create` invocation,
so this is fixed once for all ~40+ game families rather than needing a per-family edit. Deliberately
forward-only: the already-running `projectzomboid` container above was NOT re-created to pick up the cap
(doing so would mean touching another customer's live container beyond the disk-space fix it needed) — it
applies starting with the next order of any game.

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
# comment on this same step for the 2026-09-10 incident). Its output does NOT
# include public/ or .next/static/ (Next's documented behavior) — refresh
# them every promote, same as staging, or new/changed static assets are
# missing from prod until the next promote happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle since it reads .dat files off its own package path at runtime) — the
# standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace as JS-imported, so
# an externalized package's own non-JS data files are silently left behind.
# Found live 2026-09-10 on staging: this crashes EVERY request with an
# uncaught ENOENT the moment something runs the standalone server.js instead
# of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around geoip.lookup() does NOT
# help, the failure isn't confined to that call. Copy the real data/
# directory every promote, same reasoning as public/.next/static above. This
# has NOT yet bitten production because nxeon-web's systemd unit still runs
# `npm start` (next start) today, not server.js directly — but this fix must
# land before that switch happens, not after.
